title: Undefined Behaviour Catalogue
html:
Undefined behaviour (UB) means the standard places no requirements on what happens. The program may crash, print garbage, work by luck — or be “optimised” in surprising ways because the compiler assumes UB never happens.

KindMeaningExample
UndefinedAnything can happen; the whole program is invalidSigned overflow, out-of-bounds access, NULL dereference
UnspecifiedOne of several valid outcomes, not documentedOrder of evaluating function arguments
Implementation-definedDocumented choice of the compiler/platformsizeof(int), signedness of char, right shift of negatives
Locale-specificDepends on the current localeisalpha for non-ASCII bytes

The catalogue

Undefined behaviourExample
Signed integer overflowINT_MAX + 1
Division or modulo by zero; INT_MIN / -1x / 0
Shift by negative or ≥ width; left-shift of negative1 << 32, -1 << 1
Array access out of bounds (even reading)a[5] for int a[5]
Pointer arithmetic beyond one-past-the-endp + n + 1
Dereferencing NULL, dangling or misaligned pointers*(int *)NULL
Reading an uninitialised automatic variableint x; printf("%d", x);
Modifying a variable twice between sequence pointsi = i++;
Modifying a string literal or a const objectchar *s = "hi"; s[0] = 'H';
Strict-aliasing violationReading a float through an int *
Use after free, double freesee Memory Bugs
Falling off a non-void function whose value is usedmissing return
Mismatched printf format and argumentprintf("%d", 3.0)
Converting an out-of-range float to an integer(int)1e20
Data race between threadstwo threads write one variable without sync

Signed overflow

Because overflow “cannot happen”, an optimiser may turn if (x + 1 > x) into if (1) and for (int i = 0; i <= n; i++) into a loop that assumes n < INT_MAX. Check before the operation:

Strict aliasing & type punning

The compiler assumes pointers to different types don’t point to the same memory (except char *). To reinterpret bytes, use memcpy — it compiles to a single move:

Living with UB

  • Compile with -Wall -Wextra and fix every warning.
  • Test with -fsanitize=undefined,address (and thread for concurrency).
  • Use unsigned types for bit manipulation and wrap-around arithmetic.
  • Validate inputs before arithmetic, indexing and shifting.
  • -fwrapv makes signed overflow wrap (GCC/Clang) — a band-aid, not a fix.
What is undefined behaviour and why does C have it?

Behaviour for which the standard imposes no requirements. It exists so C can map directly onto very different hardware and so compilers can optimise aggressively without inserting checks (bounds, overflow, null) — the programmer promises these situations never occur.

Why can undefined behaviour 'time travel'?

Because a program that executes UB has no defined meaning at all, the optimiser may assume the UB path is never taken and reason backwards — e.g. dereferencing p before a if (p == NULL) check lets the compiler delete the check, since p “must” be non-null.

Is i = i++ undefined?

Yes (in C). i is modified twice without an intervening sequence point — once by the assignment and once by the post-increment. C11 describes this as two unsequenced side effects on the same object, which is undefined.
